needs_identified.title: water_sanitation_and_hygiene
needs_identified.description:
The NS plans to distribute items that will likely contribute to generate waste. The premise of the Gendarmerie has garbage and waste management for regular days but during the time of the stay of the affected people, it was foreseen that NS assistance would generate a significant amount of waste. The management of the intervention required to integrating the collection and smart management of waste such as empty bottles and sachets, and also sensitizing the populations on the need to keep the environment clean. Without proper management of the environmental hygiene in their room in, and knowing they were not allowed to leave that limited, it was expected that the situation would affect hygiene condition, leading to further health threat. Cleaning and sensitization activities were required to mitigate that risk. 

Furthermore, the Women and girls in reproductive age would need support for menstrual hygiene management while all the individual needed support for their personal hygiene. There was no considerations or assistance in that regard since their arrival. The risk for the hygiene condition to deteriorate was high and needed to be avoided in such situation.

needs_identified.title: health
needs_identified.description: The first assessment of the situation carried out on the shipwreck rescue day revealed  that most of the people received were injured. The need of first aid was urgent. Regular visits were necessary as well as kits to carry on with that assistance.

needs_identified.title: protection_gender_and_inclusion
needs_identified.description: Among the people affected people there are 47 female, including 5 minors. People group range from  17 to 44 years old. The context of such displacements always require a constant safeguarding to be integrated in the approach, especially as the affected people all live in a common room. It was also important for the assistance provided to be sensitive to the group represented and ensure they can maintain their dignity and safety. Continuous discussion and engagement were also needed to remain relevant.

needs_identified.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
needs_identified.description:
The assessment indicated that the affected people urgently needed non-food items for day to day use, sleeping materials, protection material. The people arrived in the ship have nothing for themselves to use to protect themselves against weather, mosquitoes or other threats. They loss the few items and assets they had in the ship accident and now needed all possible support to protect themselves. 

Being hosted currently in the Gendarmerie premises and potentially moved to another Government structure for the rest of their stay, they will still need the minimum assets to live with dignity and be able to protect themselves at least during the night.

needs_identified.title: livelihoods_and_basic_needs
needs_identified.description: Being in a foreign country with no one to take care of them, the people rescued from the shipwreck had no means to afford or even access food or household essentials like sleeping material or kitchen utensil. As they were hosted in a public space, they were not able to have cooking material, so they needed cooked food and cutleries. Concerning their basic comfort, they were in need of sleeping mats and bed sheets.

people_assisted: All 89 people rescued after the accident were targeted.
change_in_operational_strategy_text: Initially, it was planned that the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea would cook the food and serve hot meals to the affected people. As this was posing a series of issues, including the difficulty to justify the expenses for purchasing small items such as salt and spices, the NS resorted to hiring a restaurant to do the cooking and deliver it to the Red Cross for distribution. This explains why part of the cooking was done by the Red Cross, and another part was done by a restaurant.
main_donors: The major donors and partners of the IFRC-DREF include the Red Cross Societies and governments of Australia, Austria, Belgium, Britain, China, Czech, Canada, Denmark, German, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Liechtenstein, Malta, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, and the Netherlands, as well as DG ECHO, Mondelez Foundation, and other corporate and private donors. The IFRC, on behalf of the National Society, would like to extend thanks to all for their generous contributions.
icrc: ICRC covers Equatorial Guinea from its delegation based in Yaoundé. They provided food assistance to the 89 people rescued from the shipwreck during part of the first and second month of the disaster.
financial_report_description:
The operation was initially planned for 2 months. Givin the uncertainty about when the people affected were going to return to their respective countries, and the fact that there were fewer and fewer agencies assisting them, the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea requested and was granted a one-month no-cost extension of the operation during which they continued to provide hot meals to affected people. As a result of this change, the NS used all the unspent money in various lines to complement the budget for hot meals.
Moreover, the integrated approach used by the NS to implement planned activities caused some budget lines to be underspent, and others to be overspent.
operation_objective: This operation was initially intended to provide 2 months' emergency assistance to the 89 survivors of a shipwreck in Bata on 20 July 2024. This included food, essential items, first aid and protection against immediate risk associated to hygiene and safeguarding criteria for the people to be assisted. However, upon seeing that the affected people would stay beyond the initial end of the operation timeframe (September 2024), the NS requested a one-month no cost extension, which was granted in Operations update No 1, making the operation duration to be 3 months, from August to October 2024.
selection_criteria: This operation targeted the 89 people who were rescued after the shipwreck in Bata. They are all targeted as they are not from Equatorial Guinea, and they need everything having lost their belongings during the accident.
national_authorities:
Following the Shipwreck, people were rescued by the local authorities and brought to security in the Gendarmerie premises. 26th July, the authorities informed the NS of the possibility to move the affected people to another structure. A bigger existing structure from Government that have already been used to host and take care of people. But this was not done. 

The Government has not declared the emergency, but a representative called NS President to ask the NS for humanitarian assistance delivery following the accident. Following that, Local authorities granted access to the NS to visit and assist the affected people in the gendarmerie.
partner_national_society: There are no PNS in Equatorial Guinea.
event_description:
On 20 July 2024, the National President of Equatorial Guinea Red Cross was alerted by government authorities from Bata when a shipwreck occurred on 20 July 2024, before dawn. The shipwreck is said to have occurred at the Rio Campo Cribi sea border between Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon. Initially, the rescued passengers had indicated that they had been travelling since 1st July 2024, trying to reach Gabon where they had been promised jobs. However, it was confirmed during the lessons learned workshop that the boat had been stationed in the international waters between Gabon and Equatorial Guinea for almost 19 days, the captain having abandoned it with the passengers for fear of being arrested by the Equatorial Guinea authorities who could be seen from distance, thus abandoning the passengers to their fate. The lessons learned workshop also confirmed that  the boat had not been involved in an accident. Though the NS was made to believe that it was a shipwreck from the beginning of the operation. The assisted people injuries resulted from exposure to bad weather for more than two weeks, without any assistance at sea, as they were rescued after spending around 19 days in the boat without being able to move. One of the rescued passengers reported to the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea during the lessons learned workshop that the waters were shifting them slowly and it is when they eventually entered into the Equatorial Guinea territory that they were rescued by the National Gendarmerie of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea.
 The only occasion the NS had to discuss for about an hour with one of the people affected was during the lessons learned workshop. That was how the NS discovered that there was never such thing as a shipwreck.
event_scope:
The boat was carrying 90 people, including 47 women from different nationalities (30 from Benin and 17 from Togo), as well as 43 men also from different nationalities (10 from Togo, 16 from Benin, 8 Burkina Faso nationals, 2 Niger nationals, and 6 Nigerians). One of the men died, but the 89 others were rescued. Among these, some were wounded, from superficial bruises to fractures. The host National Society provided first aid services to the wounded as soon as they were alerted by government authorities (the Gendarmerie Nacional).

A rapid assessment conducted by the Equatorial Guinea Red Cros (EGRC) indicated that the 89 rescued passengers were in a small room at the Gendarmerie in Bata, initially made to accomodate 4 people. They were not allowed to move out of the gendarmerie as none of them had the Equatorial Guinea visa. They arrived with no personal effects. They urgently needed water, food, clothes, sleeping and hygiene material, mosquito nets, buckets, jerrycans and cups for drinking water. 

On 26th July, authorities indicated that the affected people would be moved to a COVID management structure, where they would have more space and intimacy. However, two months after the accident, they were still in the gendarmerie, though in a bigger room. Men and women shared the same space and created a separation themselves. They received non-food items and hot meals from consulates and local NGOs during the first month. But from September to October, only Red Cross continued providing assistance to them, assistance which stopped at the end of this operation in October 2024. Their fate is not clear, as repatriation has been discussed for a certain time with no clear outcome. As they are not allowed to leave the gendarmerie to work and have no family, they rely only on external assistance for their basic needs.

During the lessons learned workshop, the Red Cross discussed with a representative of the Consulate of Bening in Bata, one of the countries of origin of the people affected, and they said most of the affected people, at least the Beninese that they could confirm, would be repatriated to Bening before the end of October 2024. They also added that the embassies of the countries concerned had been reached and told to organize the repatriation of their nationals.
major_coordination_mechanism: The embassies and consulates of the people affected met with EG government authorities and ECCAS representatives to discuss the immediate future of the affected people. Plans to repatriate those to their respective countries were being considered by the end of this operation's timeframe, but no date was anticipated about when this will happen. However, the Beninese consulate was talking of repatriating their nationals before the end of October 2024.
un_or_other_actor:
IFRC informed the UN Resident Coordinator's Office in Malabo and while they indicated that they do not have a humanitarian component in their activities for Equatorial Guinea, they said they would be looking for possible support for this operation, probably through the various embassies involved.

Some consulates of the nationalities involved provided water for bathing, and an association of Beninese doctors started administering first aid services to their fellow citizens.

Two local NGOs have distributed some clothes to the affected people.
ifrc:
Equatorial Guinea is covered by the Yaoundé Country Cluster Delegation (Yaoundé CCD). The Cluster's program coordinator was deployed to Equatorial Guinea to support the national society. He assisted the NS with the posting of the alert on Go Platform and also helped NS staff prepare the DREF request to respond to the situation.

The President of the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea requested IFRC support to respond to this situation, as when the incident occurred, the government requested the NS to provide humanitarian support.
The Yaoundé-based Program Coordinator also acted as a surge staff deployed to Equatorial Guinea to support the NS with the implementation of this DREF operation.
risk_security_concern: There is no threat to the life of the affected people. However, their accommodation is not ideal as they are not arranged in a gender-friendly manner. However, with Government plans to relocate them to a COVID 19 site, Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea will suggest that men be separated from women.
title: Equatorial Guinea_Shipwreck in Bata
national_society_conducted_description: As this operation was happening at a time when fears of an outbreak of Mpox were on, the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea also conducted small-scale sensitization on Mpox and prevention of other epidemics, reaching the 89 people targeted by this operation and many other indirect beneficiaries in in the city of Bata.
response_strategy:
Considering the high probability that their stay would exceed 6 weeks and the NS resources deployed since the 20th, which had already been exhausted, this DREF helped cover the emergency needs encountered during the initial weeks. The allocation and design of the intervention took into account the additional support from ICRC to complement the food assistance for a month, as well as the monitoring of the context, with the expectation of receiving clarity from the Government regarding the status and protocols they would apply. At the time, the lack of clarity regarding the decisions the Government might make for the affected people made it difficult to develop further actions. Therefore, the strategy was based on requests from authorities to act and cover urgent humanitarian needs, with continued support from partners as time passed.

To address the uncovered humanitarian needs, this DREF aimed to purchase and distribute non-food items, which were critical, as the people had lost everything in the shipwreck. The items provided included single mattresses, mosquito nets, bedsheets, buckets, cups, pillows, large pots, ladles, plates, spoons, plastic garbage rolls, and kitchen knives. Some items were also provided to improve individual hygiene, such as toilet paper in the hygiene kits. Additionally, menstrual hygiene kits were distributed to 47 identified women and girls of reproductive age, alongside general hygiene items focused on waste management, such as garbage bags.

Food had been a high priority since July 20th, and NS began distributing food to the affected people. With continued needs, NS carried on with the provision of ready-to-eat rations. The most relevant intervention for the affected people was to ensure the cooking and distribution of ready-to-eat meals. For this, NS purchased food items such as liters of olive oil, boxes of condensed milk, sacks of large rice, boxes of canned tomatoes, strips of water, small boxes of turkey wings, boxes of mackerel, medium-sized bowls, packages of broth, and bags of salt. NS used these supplies to continue cooking on their premises, then distributed the meals at the gendarmerie, where the people had been hosted. Full access to distribute the assistance was granted, and NS began implementing this activity given the urgent needs. If the people were relocated and there was more flexibility for cooking in the new location (as per Government projections), NS would reassess with the Government whether it would be appropriate to transfer the cooking responsibility to them. In that case, fire safety messages would also be delivered to prevent further incidents, and regular visits would continue. NS had already started distributing food through existing resources, and this intervention would allow for reimbursement and continued assistance for at least a month, with ICRC support potentially extending the intervention.

NS ensured the prevention of key health threats related to hygiene conditions, given the people were staying on the premises and waste management risks. First aid and PFA continued for the following weeks based on the needs of each individual. Volunteer visits were utilized to deliver both.

Regular visits also served to provide integrated multi-sector awareness. Volunteers' visits included protection messages, WASH hygiene promotion, guidance on kit use, and prevention of key health threats. Hygiene promotion and environmental hygiene were particularly emphasized to encourage cleaning, waste management, and transport out of the premises and common spaces. This DREF prioritized sensitizing the affected people on the need to keep the environment clean, preventing any risks associated with negligence of basic hygiene. It also served to deliver protection messages to those affected by the accident in Bata, as well as personnel responsible for their safety. This was carried out by the Red Cross of Equatorial Guinea staff and volunteers, as they had access to the affected population.

Remote support was organized, complemented by a monitoring visit from the IFRC delegation to ensure proper closure and quality reporting of the intervention, particularly since NS had not received any DREF training since 2012.

national_society_actions.title: resource_mobilization
national_society_actions.description:
As highlighted in the initial plan of actions, RCST mobilized its Emergency Preparedness and Response Coordinator, Sughd regional branch staff and volunteers, including branches in Isfara, J. Rasulov, B. Gafurov and Rasht district to conduct needs assessments, to provide FA and Psychosocial First Aid to the most affected people. 

The Government of Tajikistan provided in-kind support to affected people in Chorkukh, Lakkon, Chilgazi, Kulkand, Zumrad, Surkh, Vorukh communities of Isfara city and Ovchikalacha and Histevarz jamoats of B. Gafurov district to enable the timely reconstruction of the damaged houses. Items delivered with this support is highlighted in the initial plan of action.  

RCST applied for DREF and ensured an allocation to support cash and voucher assistance to 92 families as well as other activities to support the affected people, reaching an overall 414 families. Significant funds were also mobilized from ICRC and ACTED to provide cash support to those affected.

national_society_actions.title: health
national_society_actions.description: So far in the implementation, the RCST has provided psychological first aid to 1,484 people who were evacuated from affected areas of Isfara town, B. Gafurov and J. Rasulov districts since the first days of the crisis.

national_society_actions.title: livelihoods_and_basic_needs
national_society_actions.description:
Overall, the National Society mobilized the below:
• 700 loaves of bread were distributed in the temporary shelters of Kulkand, Sitora and Masjidi Nav villages as well as in Isfara town, supported by ICRC. 
• 500 kg of wheat flour (for baking bread), 1000 diapers and 25 sets of wet towels were distributed for 10 temporary shelters in B. Gafurov district with the support of the ICRC. 
• 67 RCST volunteers participated in evacuation of affected people in three districts. 
• 482 evacuated residents from Isfara town, B. Gafurov and J. Rasulov district were provided with Psychological First Aid. 
• RCST Isfara town branch provided 200 medical masks and 60 antiseptic liquids for evacuees that were accommodated in public places in Isfara town. 
• 16 information sessions for 310 persons on risk of unexploded ordnances and safe behavior were conducted by RCST volunteers in affected villages on 15 September.

national_society_actions.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
national_society_actions.description:
According to the assessment results, 92 houses were fully destroyed, 322 partially damaged, 5 schools were damaged, one school was fully destroyed and two mosques were partially damaged. 

RCST branch in Isfara, with the support of ICRC, provided 700 liters of fuel for 20 vehicles (minibuses) for evacuation of local residents and excavators for cleaning of damaged houses. 

The Government of Tajikistan provided fuel and construction materials, such as 500 tons of cement, 220 square meters of timber, 5000 pieces of slate, 1500 square meters of plywood and plasterboard, 5 tons of different nails, 500 square meters of window glass and 250 tons of coal.

The National Society provided below household items from their stocks to support affected families, for which they are now requesting partial replenishment through this Operation Update:

* Mattresses -2,070 pcs (5 per HH)
* Pillows – 2,070 pcs (5 per HH)
* Quilts - 2,070 pcs (5 per HH)
* Bed-linen- 2,070 set (5 per HH)
* Kitchen sets – 414 set (1 set per HH)

national_society_actions.title: national_society_eoc
national_society_actions.description: From the first day RCST activated EOC in Dushanbe city under Leadership of the Deputy Secretary General of RCST. The members of EOC were mainly from Disaster Management, Health, NSD, Logistic and Finance Departments.

national_society_actions.title: activation_of_contingency_plans
national_society_actions.description: The RCST Contingency Plan was developed on flood and EQ responses. However, in early November 2022, the CP was updated to include two new scenarios, namely Population Movement and Epidemic/Pandemic response. The CP is expected to be finalized by end of December, 2022.

national_society_actions.title: coordination
national_society_actions.description:
The RCST and ICRC staff were mobilized in Khujand city to undertake coordination activities at regional level. In Dushanbe city, regular coordination meetings were taking place with participation of RCST, ICRC, IFRC, GRC and other partners. On September 20, 2022 a wider coordination meeting was convened by RCST inviting UN Agencies and some other external partners. The Situation Reports were developed and circulated by RCST on regular basis internally among the RCRC partners. 

On September 21, 2022 RCST management met with development partners. The meeting participants were: UN agencies, MSF, ACTED and Swiss Office. Some other partners participated online. As a result of the meeting, RCST and WHO agreed to conduct information sessions on prevention of communicable diseases among the general population in risk areas. 

• On September 22, 2022 RCST met with UNICEF, and  reviewed the planned activities in pilot districts, B. Gafurov and Isfara, specifically on Water and Sanitation, Education, Child Protection and Nutrition.
On 22 September 2022 , the meeting with a representative of the US Embassy was held. As a result of the meeting the agreement was achieved to provide medical assistance to medical centres of the target areas.
On 26 September, 2022 the coordination call with wider participation of the Movement took place. The Italian Red Cross and Turkish Red Crescent participated and expressed their readiness to support the affected people. 

The national coordination mechanism (REACT) co-led by the COES and UN has not been activated. RCST coordinated all response activities with the Committee of Emergency Situations, Sughd Regional Administration, local authorities and internal/ External Partners. RCST mobilized its Emergency Preparedness and Response Coordinator, Sughd regional branch staff and volunteers, including branches in Isfara town, J. Rasulov, B. Gafurov and Rasht districts to conduct needs assessments, to provide FA and Psychosocial First Aid to the most affected people.

national_society_actions.title: assessment
national_society_actions.description:
During the development of DREF application, the damage and needs assessment were not fully completed. Indeed, although sectoral needs were known and highlighted in the initial DREF Plan, the numbers remained uncertain.   Not to make the DREF application ineligible due to timeliness criteria, the National Society was encouraged to apply with available data. Although the needs for NFI distribution was revealed from the beginning, the quantity of HHs were not identified, therefore it was not included into the initial application. 

Once the detailed assessment was finalized jointly with the Committee of Emergency Situations and Civil Defense (CoES) branches in Sughd Province and local authorities of Isfara town and J. Rasulov district, the needs for NFIs were also identified and the National Society provided shelter related NFI to all 414 affected families. These stocks were provided from RCST`s available stocks in Sughd Province and Dushanbe warehouses. As such, this second allocation is being requested to ensure National Society replenishes distributed items.

To note, the situation at border remained volatile from 14 to 19 September, 2022. Some roads remained closed and access to affected communities was restricted to law enforcement authorities. IDPs were hosted by their relatives, and in public buildings. It was difficult to have their accurate number in initial stages. 

The similar difficulties related to identification of the number of affected households, number of fully and partially destroyed houses, destroyed livelihoods, auxiliary buildings, social infrastructure, WASH were faced during the initial dates of the conflict. The numbers kept increasing up until 27 September, 2022 as the commission was continuing conducting damage assessment.

national_society_actions.title: multi_purpose_cash
national_society_actions.description:
As planned in the initial DREF request, RCST distributed multipurpose cash at the value of 5,400 TJS (540 CHF) to the 92 most affected families who lost their houses (totally destroyed houses) in November 2022. The cash grants were distributed as a one off allocation. 

Also, after further assessments, RCST distributed multipurpose cash to the other 402 affected families, living in bordering areas with support from other Partners (ICRC and INGO "ACTED").

national_society_actions.title: community_engagement_and_accountability
national_society_actions.description: Representatives of the local communities were actively engaged in conducting assessments and identifying the needs of affected people. Also, during NFI and cash distribution, the affected communities were fully consulted and engaged.

national_society_actions.title: migration_and_displacement
national_society_actions.description: All activities in this DREF Operation were guided by best practice and principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement related to assisting and protecting migrants and displaced populations and supporting host communities. The International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement serve all those affected by internal displacement — the people actually displaced, host communities and others — and make decisions according to the most pressing needs for humanitarian services.

national_society_actions.title: education
national_society_actions.description:
A total 246 UXO risk sessions were conducted among affected population with coverage of more than 3,936 people by RCST volunteers. 

Some 22,812 evacuees left their homes during these days in Isfara, B.Gafurov, J.Rasulov and Lakhsh districts. RCST participated in evacuation of these population, which was organized by CoES and local authorities.  

At least 45 evacuees were accommodated in the NS J. Rasulov district branch. The local authorities of J. Rasulov organized the return of 1500 evacuees to their homes after situation stabilized.

national_society_actions.title: protection_gender_and_inclusion
national_society_actions.description: The PGI was integrated into emergency response and early recovery interventions based on the assessment results. It was crucial that everyone was treated fairly and with dignity, everyone has equal access to opportunities, everyone’s voices are heard, and everyone was safe from harm, NDRT teams and volunteers were supported with induction sessions to guarantee that PGI basic standards were in place and harm was not caused while providing services to the affected population.

national_society_actions.title: water_sanitation_and_hygiene
national_society_actions.description:
On 20 September 2022, RCST received 500 sets of hygiene kits from UNICEF and 39 sets from ICRC.  These kits were distributed to 414 affected HHs and 125 sets were given to vulnerable IDPs.

In addition, the National Society distributed 828 pcs of jerricans (2 pcs per HH) from its warehouse to support 414 affected families. The National Society is also requesting partial replenishment of these items through this Operation Update.

needs_identified.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
needs_identified.description:
As reported in above sections, the Government provided full support in construction of damaged and destroyed houses. In addition, with DREF support, the National Society provided 92 HHs whose homes were completely destroyed with cash support. 

In line with CVA initiative, ICRC and ACTED also supported 414 HHs with cash, which was meant to be used for restoring the shelter and auxiliary buildings.

Further assessments also highlighted the need for shelter related household items including Mattresses, pillows, quilts, bed-linens, kitchen sets, Jerry can – 828 pcs (2 pcs per HH) and family hygiene kits, which were provided by the National Society. While the family hygiene kits were provided with support from UNICEF, the other items were provided from National Society stocks, for which partial replenishment is requested through this Operation Update. The  items and numbers to be replenished include:
* Mattresses: 334 pieces to be replenished
* Pillows: 334 pieces to be replenished
* Quilts: 334 pieces to be replenished
* Bed linens: 334 pieces to be replenished
* Kitchen sets: 67 pieces to be replenished
* Jerricans: 133 pieces to be replenished

RCST will replenish the rest of distributed NFIs with other resources that will be identified later.

needs_identified.title_display: Risk Reduction, Climate Adaptation And Recovery
needs_identified.title: risk_reduction_climate_adaptation_and_recovery
needs_identified.description: During detailed assessment of the affected areas, it was revealed that recovery/reconstruction of the auxiliary buildings of the affected population was not covered. The CVA initiatives, mobilized by RCST ( DREF, ICRC, ACTED) were addressed for recovery of those auxiliary buildings and supplement house construction/rehabilitation as needed.

needs_identified.title: community_engagement_and_accountability
needs_identified.description: The RCST will ensure that affected people in the areas of operations are included in the response and recovery process, consulted regarding their needs, and understand what and why the assistance is being provided, to whom and the selection criteria. Hygiene promotion campaigns will be based on community participation with active engagement and involvement of affected people. Post distribution monitoring will include satisfaction and quality elements to ensure data collected reflects recipients’ experiences of RCST services and activities, and provide guidance for identification of best practice and future adaptation and improvement. Appropriate feedback and response mechanisms will be in place to ensure people affected by the emergency and RCST activities can effectively and in a timely manner provide feedback and raise issues, and that this is acted on, with resulting actions reported back to individuals and communities.

needs_identified.title: environment_sustainability
needs_identified.description: The RCST will further lead needs assessment, but at this stage no needs were identified related to environmental sustainability.

needs_identified.title: protection_gender_and_inclusion
needs_identified.description: All PGI related aspects were covered during the response activities. No additional needs identified.

needs_identified.title: health
needs_identified.description:
Mental health and psychosocial support were highlighted as one of the main health needs for the affected communities. The mental health component is not fully integrated into the health services network and primary care system has little capacity to respond. Psychological support is usually provided by doctors and it is perceived only as a psychological consultation and mental health care. The RCST is coordinating the MHPSS activities ICRC. 

Recognizing the need for increasing awareness of risks of infectious diseases among the displaced people, the WHO country office is collaborating with the RCST to disseminate 40,000 information materials with messages on disease prevention and pre-hospital care. 

The ICRC is considering support for B. Gafurov district hospital with additional medical instruments and materials, in response to the hospital’s request. The WHO has included PPE for all RCST staff and volunteers who will be mobilized for this response, under their support to RCST for dissemination of health information materials.

needs_identified.title: water_sanitation_and_hygiene
needs_identified.description: At the launch of this operation, people had to flee their homes with little to no warning, hence they had no time to collect their essential items from their houses, including basic hygiene items and the displaced people were lack essential hygiene items now. The RCST identified that hygiene kits, dignity kits  and access to drinking water and sanitation facilities as the main WASH needs for the affected population.

needs_identified.title: education
needs_identified.description:
The needs remain as follows and as highlighted in initial DREF request:
•   Rehabilitation of three schools in Isfara town and provision of education materials 
•   Provision of books and school items for 414 families.

needs_identified.title: migration_and_displacement
needs_identified.description: The conflict forced over 22,000 people in four target districts to leave their houses (evacuated), leaving behind all their belongings and livelihoods. With support of international partners and local authorities most of the evacuated people have returned home at the moment of updating this operation.

indicators.title: Number of families provided with Public multipurpose CVA

planned_interventions.description:
• The priority actions include the following: 
- Under Emergency Appeal project, the SoP on provision of CVA was developed. This SoP will be adjusted under current initiative and will be activated for use in this response.
- Verify the list of affected families through digital data collection system/KoBo
-  Agree on mode on cash transfer and to initiate appropriate procurement procedures based on IFRC standards.
- conduct quick refreshers on CVA, CVA IM data collection and protection, CEA, PGI and MHPSS in emergencies, monitoring 
- request IFRC CVA surge support, 
- Cash payment in amount of CHF 540 per family calculated based on the following transfer value calculation:

An average family consists out of 5 people whereas the parents and one older family member are working. Due to the crisis and the need to rebuild the destroyed houses most of the affected working age population is not fully engaged in work but supporting the reconstruction works of their houses. To cover a part of most urgent needs and in absence of an official Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), three times the minimum salary per family (3xTJS 600) are the average transfer value multiplied by three months (3xTJS 1,800 = TJS 5,400 / CHF 540 for 3 months). An incremental value as per family size is under discussion.
- ensure that information on feedback channels among beneficiaries is shared, where any information on abuse, MHPSS needs and fraud can be informed 
   - ensure that risks are taken into account and mitigation measures are addressed. 
- conduct post-distribution monitoring and client satisfaction survey.

The list was coordinated and agreed with local authorities and CoES in affected areas. Each of these families received 5,400 TJS (540 CHF). 
The details are the following:
-	76 families in Isfara town on November 16, 2022;
-	16 families in B. Gafurov district on November 19, 2022.

planned_interventions.description:
• Integrate CEA across the response so staff and volunteers have the knowledge and capacity to engage communities effectively by providing CEA in emergencies briefings and training for volunteers and staff collecting feedback

•	Keep communities well informed about operation plans, progress, activities, selection criteria and distribution processes, delays and challenges, and their rights and entitlements

•	Ensure the response is based on a thorough understanding of community needs, priorities, and socio-cultural context, including preferred ways to receive information, participate and give feedback by including CEA in undergoing assessments 
•	Establish a multi-channel feedback mechanism to collect, respond to, and use community feedback to guide the response
planned_interventions.progress_towards_outcome: RCST coordinated all response activities (CoES, local hukumats/authorities and community leaders) including conducting assessment, preparation of lists, distribution of NFIs and hygiene kits. The assessment was conducted jointly with Emergency Commission, which consisted of CoES, local authorities and other relevant entities. Based on the result of the assessment, considering the needs of the people, the list of affected population was compiled. The list of beneficiaries for NFI distribution was agreed with all parties.

indicators.title: Number of training for RC volunteers in community-based health, basic psychosocial support (psychological first aid) and hygiene promotion

planned_interventions.description:
• Community-based health promotion and first aid awareness activities for displaced people, covering the same families targeted under CVA: The focus of these activities will be on prevention of vaccine preventable diseases, ARI, water borne infections, and maternal and child health, depending on the age and gender structures of targeted families and their health information needs. These activities will be done not as a stand-alone intervention but integrated into community mobilization by volunteers when they visit temporary settlements and affected households for CVA distribution. 
-	Providing basic psychosocial support (psychological first aid) integrated into these activities: Psychological first aid is an integral part of community-based health activities and will be offered where needed, in close coordination with the ICRC and other actors on the ground. 
-	1 day training for RC volunteers in community-based health, basic psychosocial support (psychological first aid) and hygiene promotion, using existing eCBHFA tools from the RCST’ CBHFA project, adapted to the context. 
-	Printing of eCBHFA flipcharts for health education sessions

•	RCST jointly with ICRC conducted MHPSS support group sessions for 69 staff members of 9 medical centers;  
•	RCST jointly with ICRC conducted MHPSS activities with 92 children of affected schools in age range between 7 and -9 years;
•	Single sessions with 16 families of deceased persons in Ovchi Qalacha and Vorukh.

RCST jointly with ICRC conducted MHPSS  for affected families whose houses were destroyed and families with deceased family members.
